subject: gk
question:
Read the given statements and select the correct option regarding ‘High Powered Money’.

(i) High Powered Money consists of currency and cash reserves with the bank.

(ii) High Powered Money includes demand deposits of the banks.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (i) is true**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• High Powered Money, also known as the monetary base, consists of currency in circulation and cash reserves held by the banks.
 
• It includes the total currency issued by the central bank and held by the public plus the deposits held by commercial banks with the central bank.
 
• Demand deposits are not included in High Powered Money; they are part of the broader money supply categories such as M1, M2, etc.
 
• High Powered Money is crucial because it serves as the foundation upon which the money supply is built through the banking system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monetary Base (High Powered Money)**

 
 
• It is the sum of currency in circulation and reserves held by banks with the central bank.
 
• It is a critical measure used by central banks to control the money supply and manage economic stability.
 
 
 
• **Money Supply**
 
 
• The total amount of monetary assets available in an economy at a specific time.
 
• Common measures of money supply include M1 (currency and demand deposits), M2 (M1 plus savings deposits), etc.
 
 
 
• **Central Bank Reserves**
 
 
• Deposits that commercial banks hold with the central bank as part of their required reserves.
 
• These reserves are used to meet the liquidity needs and regulatory requirements.
 
 
 
• **Currency in Circulation**
 
 
• The physical money (coins and paper currency) held by the public and businesses, excluding the reserves held by banks.
 
• It forms part of the broader money supply and is directly controlled by the central bank.
